summary.title: Things I will tell my kids if they become entrepreneurs
summary.one_liner: A slide-deck of startup advice arguing that execution, team, product and luck matter more than the original idea, with notes on feedback, hiring, fundraising, focus and competition.
takeaways: Execution, product and team matter more than the initial idea; the idea is a small part of success.
Balance customer feedback against a clear vision, and be wary of friends and surveys that give untruthful answers.
Choose co-founders carefully (2-3 is often best), clarify equity and roles on day one, and hire people better than yourself.
Look for opportunities in new technologies, slow incumbent industries and fringe users, and ask 'why now?'.
Competition is a sign of a market; big companies are often slow, and focus plus a clear strategy matter more than chasing every opportunity.
summary.summary: This is a long slide presentation (127 slides) of advice for aspiring entrepreneurs, framed as things the author would tell their children. It is organized by topic: idea, team, fundraising, execution, market, competition, and money and risk. Most points are short bullet statements backed by examples from companies such as Google, Amazon, Facebook, Uber and Airbnb, plus quotes from figures like Steve Jobs, Paul Graham and Peter Thiel. The page text provided covers roughly the first 111 slides; the remaining slides are not included in the text.
